utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, the Defence has one session and a half, and that's the new sessions, that's approximately the one hour and a half, to conclude its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kingori. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Stojanovic will now continue his cross-examination. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Colonel, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We shall proceed from where we broke off yesterday, as we adjourned. I would just like you to confirm a fact for me, namely, that on the 9th of July, 1995, you left Srebrenica and went to the UNPROFOR base in Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Potocari, you did not have any direct perception anymore in terms of gathering information for your headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, at one point in time you made the following decision: Believing that this was justified from a security point of view, you sent to Srebrenica Emir Suljagic, a local interpreter who worked for you. You sent him to Srebrenica so that he could inform you about what was going on there; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you personally cannot stand by the information that you provided to north-east headquarters in Tuzla in your reports dated the 9th, 10th, and 11th of July, because you could not see any of that yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask you how you can stand by something that you are writing in your report without having seen it yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, whatever report we were getting from Emir Suljagic and also any other source that we could get, we could try to verify. But in our report when we were sending to our headquarters, we used to indicate that it's not confirmed by us, but that does not mean that it was necessarily wrong or erroneous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just a matter as far as the transcript is concerned. I read to you what we now find page 2, line 6: Upon arriving in Potocari, you did not have any direct -- did you then say perception or did you say reception? - anymore in terms of gathering information?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But which of the two, please, perception or reception?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perception. He could not directly perceive what was going on in Srebrenica because he went to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the answer was: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, please go ahead. You say that you can stand by the reports dated the 9th, 10th, and 11th, although they are not based on your very own direct observation of these things in Srebrenica. How come?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was based on the knowledge that we knew our interpreter head and the fact that we were hearing also the shells heading towards Srebrenica. So the only thing maybe that we could have doubted is on the type of weapon that was used. But as to whether the rockets, shells, or whatever, went to Srebrenica, at least even ourselves we could hear, so we knew it was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of this reporting of yours from the shelter in Potocari, did you inform headquarters that this was unverified information as far as you personally were concerned?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would, first of all, seek a clarification on what you mean by "shelter"? Because though we were in Potocari, we were not in a bunker, we were outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having clarified this, could you then please further answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to repeat this once again. This is what I'm asking you, Mr. Kingori: In the information that you provided for the 10th of July to headquarters, did you say that this was unverified information as far as you personally were concerned?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, information that we were sending to the headquarter and we could not be able to verify ourselves personally, we used to indicate: Not confirmed by UNMOs, that is, "NCBU."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 65 ter 04004452, page 3 of the English version and pages 5 and 6 of the B/C/S version. Your Honours, while we're waiting, may I say that this is a report that the headquarters of military observers sent to their headquarters in Zagreb and which has attached the information that Mr. Kingori's team provided for the 9th and 10th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, your first report which you entitled a current report from Srebrenica, you say that the shelling of Srebrenica is still going on, and then you repeat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please tell us in which paragraph of this document we find what you're referring to. Is it the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am moving from paragraph 1 on page 3 to the second paragraph, where there is a reference to shells, 150-millimetre artillery shells; and then the third paragraph where there's a reference to shelling of the town of Srebrenica for the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking you now, Mr. Kingori: Where can one see anything to the effect that this is information that has not been verified by you as observers, but that this is second-hand information as far as you're concerned, unverified, not confirmed, as you said?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, let's start with paragraph 1 that you mentioned. We are talking about over a hundred shells, which we could be able to see or hear passing by. Secondly, we have also indicated that we got a report from DutchBat, it's indicated there. And I don't think there's anything else that we require to even put as NCBU, because everything we could be able to hear or get the information from DutchBat and is indicated. If you go to I think that para that you talked about, this we could be able to count ourselves. We did not necessarily have to rely on Emir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, could we move to the second paragraph, which was also brought to your attention, which start reading: "Two heavy shells, probably 155-millimetre artillery shells ..." Could you tell us what was the source of your knowledge that you could tell they were 155-millimetre artillery shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, this could have come from Emir and I can see we did not indicate NCBU on that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask you because there is no reference whatsoever to this being unconfirmed, as you said; however, you said that one of the sources of your knowledge and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, this is comment. Please, next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that one of the sources of your information was the counting of shells, or rather, the counting of gun-shots that you could hear in Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was one way of getting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to take a look at a video clip from the Srebrenica trial video that we received from the Prosecution, 65 ter video-clip --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what do you mean by "Srebrenica trial video"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document that we received in segments and that we call -- that we gave a working name, the Srebrenica trial video, and it has a 65 ter number and we dealt only with particular clip, as the Prosecution did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that part of the same video as parts were shown yesterday? Mr. Vanderpuye, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am on my feet, only because in respect of the document that is now in e-court, Mr. Stojanovic asked Colonel Kingori specifically with respect to the sources of information then informed that report. He's asked him about the first three paragraphs and there's a fourth paragraph which speaks directly to the witness's attribution of that information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you can deal with that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Perhaps I will. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honour, 65 ter is V00044581A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will ask you to take a look at this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't hear any sound, but I'm just going to ask you very briefly, Mr. Kingori. Shall we agree that this is video footage of the town of Srebrenica on the 10th of July? You do recognise the area, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I recognise the area. It's Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And will we agree that the people who were literally in the town of Srebrenica on the 10th of July were being hit by mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't get what you mean because on the video we could see somebody firing from within to outside with a mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that you did not observe that directly and could not observe that directly because on that day you were already in Potocari; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I mean. What I'm saying is from the video one can see somebody firing to outside, but that we did not hear. We did not comment on that. But when we were in Potocari we could be able to hear incoming fire, fire that was coming through overhead where we were or coming through another direction but coming in to Srebrenica, that we could be able to count. But this one we did not hear ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there's rather some confusion. First of all, let's keep matters strict. You said: Do you agree with me that this is Srebrenica on the 10th of July? The witness said: I recognise the area. Do you know whether it was the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know for sure. I just said I recognised the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so therefore the date -- at least this witness - I'm not saying that it's not - that has not been established. Then what exactly now was your question, Mr. Stojanovic? It was not entirely clear to me, and apparently not also to the witness, so then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These detonations, could you hear them in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I'm getting lost. Which detonations? Because you have already indicated about two. I have seen one outgoing. Initially you were talking about incoming, now which ones are you talking about, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic is the one who asked the questions. The initial question, Mr. Stojanovic, you put to the witness, whether the witness would agree that in the town of Srebrenica on the 10th of July, that people were being hit by mortar shells. And then the witness answered: I'm confused because what I see is not people hit by but I see firing of shells. Now, if we are talking about detonations, are we talking about detonations of shells that were fired into Srebrenica or are we talking about firing of shells, as the witness said he saw on the video, that is, next to this -- what seems to be a gas station, that first we see a plume of smoke and then later, coming closer to it, we see people -- what seems to be mortar -- now, please put a clear question to the witness because the witness is confused about incoming and outgoing shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honours, that the entire misunderstanding is due to misinterpretation of the part where my question was not whether people were being hit, but whether there was shooting from that point. But I think you understand what I'm getting at so I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I want to put a simple question to you, Mr. Kingori. You call this outgoing fire and there were four shells that were fired, and we can see this in this footage - and if necessary we can repeat this once again - could you hear and register these sounds in Potocari where you were, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- whether it was four or not, whether we have to replay that -- apparently the issue Mr. Stojanovic wants to put to you is: Could you hear outgoing fire in Srebrenica from your position at Potocari? Could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could not, and especially bearing in mind that outgoing could have been going to a different direction, not towards Potocari. If it is fired towards a different direction, like I suspect now it could have been to the west of Srebrenica, it was difficult for us to hear it from Potocari. But incoming, because it was coming in and then detonating, it was very easy to hear from Potocari, but this one was detonating elsewhere far, so we could not hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know it was detonating elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because obviously if you're firing towards another direction, the detonation will be there, not where you're firing from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could you observe in any way in which direction the firing took place, in which direction the shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's difficult to determine, but what I'm saying is if it was being fired outside, towards the west or any other direction other than overhead, Potocari, it was difficult for us to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, but you do not know in which direction firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, you cannot know for sure, but bearing in mind that these were now Muslims firing towards the Serbs, and we knew the general direction of the Serbs, is that most likely they could have been firing a certain direction, so it was difficult for us to hear if it was not fired overhead Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If you allow me, just brief consultation with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours, for your help.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, you saw in this video footage an artillery piece. On the basis of your experience and knowledge, can you tell us what kind of artillery piece this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for the video-clip to be replayed, at least the part when the shells are being fired. And then if we can also hear the sound, then perhaps they can be counted too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Kingori. You can see this artillery piece. If you can, according to your knowledge, can you tell us what sort or what type of artillery this is?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, too me this looks like a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you say that I'm right that it could possibly be an 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be because this is slightly bigger than 60, so it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you say that I'm right if I say that if we adhere to the demilitarisation agreement, this kind of artillery piece could not have possibly in any way whatsoever be in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, depending on the date of this video, it could have been after we had left Srebrenica, and maybe they had even taken their weapons, the heavy weapons from the Bravo Company of the Dutch compound. It's possible. Anything could have happened. I don't know when this was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have information that this footage was taken on the 10th, but that could be irrelative, therefore I'm not going to ask you anything else about this. Now, let me ask you this: Was UNPROFOR maintaining communication with superior HQ that had surveillance systems that could identify and locate the source of artillery fire, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not. What I knew was what we were doing ourselves, trying to locate these heavy weapons, but if the use of satellite was ongoing elsewhere, I did not know. That was not at my level.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If your interpreter, Emir Suljagic, was in Srebrenica and if we are talking about the 10th of July, could he have heard those mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he was in Potocari, definitely he should have heard this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, in the previous episode we learned incoming fire, detonation upon impact, and the sound of mortars being fired, that may be different what you can hear and what you cannot hear. Now, you put a question without making any distinction here. So would you please be clear, apart from if he was there and if we are talking, would he have heard. That is -- it reminds me of some literature which, ifs and ifs, I mean -- that's a -- that's not asking the witness for knowledge or his personal observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, on page 12, line 24 of the transcript, my question was quite clear on the understanding that Mr. Kingori was in Potocari and that he couldn't hear the outgoing fire, but he did that Emir Suljagic was in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, there's no need to start a debate when I give you guidance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So my question was: Could one hear these shots in Srebrenica, where E mir Suljagic was on that day? Maybe we have a problem with the interpretation again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem that I notice from the answers that were given, sir, is that you asked indeed at page -- line 24, page 12: "If your interpreter was in Srebrenica and if we are talking about the 10th of July, could he have heard those mortar shells?" The answer was: "Your Honour, if he was in Potocari, definitely he should have heard this." So the witness is talking about Potocari, your question relates to Srebrenica, so can you clear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honours, and I just repeated my question: If Emir Suljagic was in Srebrenica on that day, could he have heard this outgoing fire in Srebrenica? And the answer could be either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, would you please answer the question, to the extent you're able to do; and if not, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he was in Srebrenica, as I said earlier, he could have heard that -- that fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He would have heard the sound of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- outgoing mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at document -- but before that, I would like to tender into evidence the report that we used together with this document, 65 ter 04452 and this video-clip, which is marked V00044581A, 81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, with respect to 65 ter 4452, I would note that this is one of the associated exhibits to the witness's statement, and I think we had held an abeyance on the determination on the admissibility of those documents until either at the end of his testimony or at some other point. The second is that the video-clip that was played is part of the trial video in this case which is 65 ter 26123, and it is simply an extraction or an excerpt of that video-tape. But rather than have all of these things, I think piecemeal, it might be better to admit the trial video, that's also part of the video footage that I played to the witness in direct examination, so that we don't have this all spread out in different places and repeated throughout the evidence in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might be good that if it's all one video that we have it in one piece and that's always clearly indicated what portion is played at that moment. If the parties could agree on that, then we'll receive the video in its entirety, but please discuss it briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we need a clear indication which part was played to this witness during cross-examination, which part of the trial video, because that is not in the transcript. You didn't indicate from which part to which part you played this video for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What footage -- could you give us the indications of what was played? I see on the screen, perhaps I read it, what apparently was played was from 4 minutes, 43 seconds, to 6 minutes, 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I now read on the screen and apparently that is what was played. Yes. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems that the parties have already anticipated in the entirety of the video to be admitted into evidence because the separate portions played are not uploaded as such in e-court. Please sit together with Madam Registrar during one of the next breaks and sort this out in such a way that we never have any problems in understanding what was played from what video and what is in evidence and what is separate or as a whole. Please proceed. We now will look at another portion, which -- is this the portion on the screen which is going to be played or was it the portion that has been played, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the footage that we have already played, but we are going to use another portion. But please allow me to say that concerning this video footage, we're going to discuss this with the Prosecution because there are a number of compilations, but nevertheless we need to agree which ones are going to be used. Thank you. Let's move on. Now I'd like to call up document 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But most important for us to know is what portion will be played now, starting at what time, ending at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, everybody saw the minutes indication on the screen, it's 4.46 up to 6.02, if I'm not wrong, so that footage that we had already had an occasion to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you apparently are about to play another portion, apparently you are not what I understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter document 17897, chapter 4, page 2 in English and page 2 in B/C/S. And let us focus on paragraph 3 in English. Your Honours, this is a report compiled by NIOD that precisely addresses the issue on investigating the Srebrenica events.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, this is what it says, inter alia, in paragraph 3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel please be more precise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking you to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read more slowly. "They left the base only after the fall of the enclave. The fact that they sent their interpreter, Emir Suljagic, back to Srebrenica with a Motorola walkie-talkie to count and report on the shell bursts did not leave a good impression ... some DutchBat soldiers liked to call UNMOs 'UNBOs,' standing for 'UN Bunker Observers,' because 'when something had to be observed these people were sitting in the bunkers.' Two interpreters also said later that the UNMO hardly ever tried to set foot outside the door and very much relied on them (the interpreters)." Now I'm asking you this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now my question is: As far as your engagement is concerned, is this a summary or is this account correct or not?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is erroneous for various reasons. One of them, it's evident that we did observe when we were in Srebrenica, even when the shelling was ongoing. We were reporting from Srebrenica before we headed to Potocari. We wrote everything we did while in Srebrenica on account of what we saw, what we analysed, and we could not have seen and analysed from a bunker. Secondly, when we left Srebrenica and headed to Potocari, really even when you see in the video, we are not in a bunker, that is not a bunker. When we were meeting General Ratko Mladic, we were not in a bunker, he didn't come to a bunker; we were outside. So we could be able to hear missiles, rockets, artillery pieces or weapons, they were being fired overhead. We could even see them flying overhead. We could not have done that from a bunker. So for sure, this is quite erroneous and one-sided, which, to me, it's misleading and maybe that's why you are referring to it. Maybe I can add a third one in that these two interpreters, who are these? Because the two that we had we were with -- in constant touch with Emir Suljagic, other than Hasan Muhanovic who decided to be -- to stay outside of the UNMO family, but we were with Emir throughout. And even when he was reporting from Srebrenica, we are the ones who had sent him there. And not everything that we were reporting came from Emir, most of it came from us, ourselves, in Potocari --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would kindly ask that we try and be brief. I only put to you what the Dutch Institute had said. Let's look at the last sentence in this paragraph where it reads: "Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans also made a vain attempt to send them back to Srebrenica: 'When that failed, I sent my own Liaison Officer team.'" My question is: Do you recall that you had been requested to return to Srebrenica instead of having your interpreters there, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question cannot be answered by yes or no. The answer I can give is, first and foremost, Colonel Karremans was not in charge of us. He was the DutchBat commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether he is in charge or not, I can ask someone to do something even if I have no competence to do so. I can ask the local gas station to sell me sugar. That is not an answer. You can answer the question whether he requested -- whether you had been requested to return to Srebrenica instead of doing something else. You can answer that question, whether it was requested. Whether it was rightly requested, whether there was someone who should not have asked it that, that's another matter, but you can answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was in the process of answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I was saying is Colonel Karremans knows very well there is a time we went back - and is on record - with him from Potocari to Srebrenica for a meeting with the Muslim leadership. It is on record and the sitreps are there and it is in my statement. We went there, had a meeting with the Chief of Staff, and went back to Potocari. Secondly, there is a time we went to Srebrenica with an MSF lady called Christina and to pick the injured, so obviously we went back to Srebrenica after that. We were not afraid of going there, and even those two times that we went there, firing was still ongoing, we were not afraid, we were not hiding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you returned to Srebrenica, were you requested to do so; and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are two occasions, Your Honour. One is when we went back for a meeting with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But were you requested? You are describing what you did. The question is about whether you were asked to do something; that's not the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were requested by Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And we went there for a meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And it is on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second occasion that we went back was when we were requested by -- I think Christina, a lady from MSF, and we went back to pick the injured who were -- the sick who are in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So twice you went back, once at the request of Mr. Karremans and once at the request of Christina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, can we just ask the witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When was it that you returned to Srebrenica in compliance with Colonel Karremans' request? What was the date and did you make any reference to that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's indicated very well that we went back there because there were two issues to discuss, and it is so indicated. One of them was the ultimatum that had been given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, could you give the dates. That's what you were asked to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dates, I cannot remember them very well but I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember them very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Did the two occasions when you returned, are they found in your statement? That was the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them are in my earlier -- in my statement and some of them are in the evidence I've already given before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, will you agree with me that between the 9th and the 13th you did not go back to Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is wrong, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm not going to insist on this because this information is contained in your reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, no comment. Questions to the witness. That is what examination of a witness means. At a later time you can argue on the basis of other matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to have the NIOD report admitted into evidence, number 17897 according to 65 ter rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objections? Because the NIOD report -- I think it was chapter 4 only which was, if I'm not mistaken -- do you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you don't want the NIOD report but chapter 4 of the NIOD report. Mr. Vanderpuye, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. It's a very lengthy report - isn't it? - or it's many, many pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we have dealt with one page and nevertheless you seek to be admitted into evidence the whole chapter?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. If an instruction is that we can extract only one page from that document, as we did during the previous examination, we would like this page from chapter 4 to be given a number and to have it admitted into evidence as such in order not to overburden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With respect to the tendering of the single page, I would object to that because I think it presents, let's say, a distorted picture of what the chapter discusses -- because you can see, actually, at the bottom of the page that chapter is beginning to discuss the UNMO's point of view with respect to the issues that Mr. Stojanovic has put to the witness. And I think to present simply the one page to the exclusion of the rest would distort the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't give any -- instructions to come, but one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are hereby instructed that the party which tenders the document carefully considers what portion of the document we would need, then consult with the other party to see whether the other party considers it's necessary to have for contextualisation a broader portion. Then agree on what finally is the selection. If there's disagreement, the Chamber will rule on it, but preferably that you come together and say page this to that, that's what we'd like to have in evidence. So we'll reserve a number for the selection still to be made from chapter 4 of the NIOD report and we hear from the parties what portion exactly it is that we are requested to admit into evidence. Madam Registrar, the number reserved for that purpose would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The reserved number would be D20, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D20 is still to be filled in. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at this moment I take it that it's the whole of the report still, but it should be reduced. So D20 will be the number of what is now chapter 4 and what will be reduced to a portion of chapter 4. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be careful about the time that I have left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's go once again through P34, which is your 65 ter statement. I'd like to have paragraph 135 in English, page 30, in B/C/S page 41. Mr. Kingori, while we're waiting for this document to be uploaded, I would like just to remind you and ask you the following. You say that at one point on the 11th of July you were at a meeting in Bratunac with Major Nikolic and Colonel Vukovic. And you think that Mr. Den Haan was with you on that occasion. I'd like to ask you this, although you were asked that same question by the Prosecution, could you remember which route you took on the 11th of July in order to reach Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the route we took was the normal one, through a place we called Yellow Bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we had a new schedule, which means one hour, 20 minutes' break. We'll take that break now. After the break you have another half an hour. We take a break but could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll like to see everyone back in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic, there was some confusion about the number you mentioned at one moment. You once mentioned 65 ter 14004452, but we do understand that you want to refer to 65 ter 4452, which is UNMO headquarters BH sector NE daily situation report dated the 10th of July, 1995, at 0001, that was on the associated exhibit list, but I do understand that you wanted to tender that as well. Therefore, perhaps we assign a D number. Madam Registrar, that would receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 04452 becomes Exhibit D21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence because if it was on your associated exhibit list, Mr. Vanderpuye, then I could not imagine any objections. D21. Is there any reason why the witness is not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may continue your cross-examination. You've got half an hour left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, if you remember I asked you about a meeting that you attended on the 11th of July in Bratunac. My question is whether this meeting was held before the NATO bombing of the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska or afterwards, on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the meeting was held after the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Court, to the best of your knowledge, who was it that guided the NATO air force towards the positions of the VRS? Whose mandate was this?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, ourselves, we had just given the grid references of the areas we thought the weapons of the BSA were, but on as to who guided the aircrafts, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me whether in your reports to headquarters you provided information about that, namely, that you were at this meeting in Bratunac on the 11th after the NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was initially a request for a meeting before the air-strikes and we were told not to go. We were advised by our headquarters not to go because we could have been taken as human shields, but after the air-strikes we were allowed to go because it was now over. There were no more air-strikes planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand the question to be whether you reported about your presence during that meeting to your headquarters. Mr. Stojanovic, is that well understood? Then could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I'm going to repeat my question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you submit a report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've put a question, the witness did not apparently understand the question rightly, I repeated it and I invited the witness to answer the question. Did you report to headquarters your presence during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If you allow me for time-saving purposes, I would like to tender 65 ter 04457, which is on the list of the Prosecution as well, and these are all the summary reports of the mission in Srebrenica for the 11th, and we can see from there whether reports were sent or not. Having said that, I can move on to my next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "all the reports." I see UNMO report dated the 11th of July, 1995, 0001 hours, which seems to be a three-page document. Is that correct, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 04457 becomes Exhibit D22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, I shall try to deal briefly with your testimony regarding your meeting with General Mladic on the 12th of July. I just have a few more brief questions in relation to that. You said that it was in the afternoon. Now I'm asking you whether this meeting or contact with General Mladic was before, during, or after the arrival of buses in the area of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the initial meeting was before the arrival of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your assessment, how much time had elapsed between these two meetings of yours with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't exactly say how long, but it was not very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately in so many hours, was it one hour, five hours, thirty minutes, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For sure it was on and off. We could briefly meet, then I would leave, I would come back, we would meet again. But together I think we were there for about two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The separation that you spoke about, did that start before the buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've spoken about two separations. Which one does he mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the separation which one, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the first process that you spoke about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the adult men being separated from the women, the children, and the elderly?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. The second one was when the buses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first one was done before General Mladic arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you care to elaborate on your view of this separation? Before General Mladic arrived and before the buses arrived, where were they taken? Were they guided in a particular direction? And how were they separated from this mass of people? Could you please describe how you saw that.

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the men were being picked one by one from the group that was outside there and led towards a white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers who were singling them out, did they walk into the mass or did they call out their names in front of the white tape that we saw?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I've just answered. They were being picked from the mass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not by name as I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not by name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did this process start in terms of General Mladic's arrival, how much earlier was that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The conversation with General Mladic that has to do with your complaint regarding the position of the people in the building that you called the white house, that was not recorded; right?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's difficult for me to answer that. I don't know why it was not recorded or whether it was recorded at all. Even what we are seeing, I didn't know everything was recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I appreciate if my colleague perhaps clarify what he means by "recorded," --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- whether video or written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It came to my mind as well. Recording could be anything, Mr. Stojanovic; that could be audio recorded, that could be video recorded, but that could also be to write it down on a piece of paper. Perhaps with this clarification the witness could tell us whether he was aware of any audio recording. Were you, Mr. Kingori?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the video recording, we knew it was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see the video people going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I was asking about the audio recording, you have answered the question for the video recording. You knew that video recording was ongoing, but you were not the ones who were in control of that recording?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were not. It was under the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you write it down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not. We did not indicate that there was a recording going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I meant to say was did you put down on paper that conversation for yourself, for example, in your own diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a way of recording as well. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm going to ask you: Did you see in any one of your testimonies until now, did you see any kind of video or audio recording of the conversation you had with General Mladic in respect of your complaint about the position of people in the building that you called the white house?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, so far I've not seen, but I've seen myself complaining through one of the interpreters, who was to take the information to General Mladic; and we were following each other after General Mladic and he told him what I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I would like to ask for us to view this recording together. It seems to me that what you said just now pertains to the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please view once again V0 0044581A, the time from 158 until 159.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, will we agree that in this footage there is no recording of you telling the interpreter about the situation in the white house?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this record it's not indicated, but I don't think they were filming everything that was being said by everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you that precisely because a few moments ago in your answer you said that that had been recorded; that is to say, when you were saying that to the interpreter. So let us agree that what you said was not recorded on the 12th of July, 1995; rather, it was on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think even the Honourable President asked me about the recording, and when I said I put it in my diary, he agreed that it was also a form of recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is whether in this footage was just played, whether you see or hear any moment where your complaints are either communicated to the interpreter or by the interpreter to Mr. Mladic. That's the simple question, whether we see it or -- and/or whether we can hear it here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the last question I answered I said: No. I did not -- I cannot see it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped the video here because I wish to ask you the following. You said that a young man was interpreting and you identified him as a person who had good English and you identified him during the direct examination by Mr. Vanderpuye. Is this the young man who is interpreting in this footage and that you see standing next to General Mladic, who is working there as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the person I identified as an interpreter was wearing a blue jacket, a blue UN jacket although he was from BSA, so I don't think he is this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can you help us to indicate where you stopped the video, which is the time? So that we have it on the record which frame you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was 1.59.35. That is at least what you indicated and that is what we saw on the screen, Mr. Stojanovic. Is -- have we seen all that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, I assure you that the person you described as an interpreter who was interpreting your conversation with General Mladic does not exist in this video footage. And the interpreter who interpreted that day in General Mladic's communications is the man standing next to him in this clip. And could we please continue playing this video footage and then you will see that this person is indeed interpreting. So can we please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, we've replayed this for a simple reason. Let me ask you this: At any point in time did you see the person that you described as an interpreter with a blue flak jacket, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not see him there, but I did not say he was an interpreter for the BSA. If you follow through the way I've said about that interpreter, it's somebody I identified outside -- you know, from the BSA side, not necessarily the one who was interpreting for General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you just played what exactly? Please give 65 ter numbers if you have one; and if it is portion of a larger video, give us the exact times you played.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would like to tender this. 65 ter V000 -- or rather, 1D0082, according to 65 ter, that is to say the time from 1.57.00 to 1.59.36. And the video is V00044581A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the number the Prosecution uses internally. Now, please assist me. The last portion you played you say is from 1.57 to 1.59.36, that is, 2 minutes and 36 seconds. Would you agree, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I look at my screen, we are at 1 minute, 30, and apparently not the whole of this has been played. So how do you reconcile 1 minute and 30 seconds with two hours -- 2 minutes and 36 seconds?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the information that I had and last night, or rather, the night before last, when we worked on this video footage, it runs from 1.57.00 -- I do apologise, 1.58.00, 1.58.00 through 1.59.35. Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the description in e-court is incorrect. We just looked at 1D00082 for a little bit over 1 minute and 30 seconds, and that is part of the bigger video. Perhaps if at any moment in the near future you could identify which portion of the bigger video this was so that we have a clear record later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I have to insist, I would like to know where you stopped the video and at which point in time we could look at the still. That was not the part my honourable colleague put on the record; it was at a different time. We need the correct description of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the still was a couple of seconds before the end of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was the second still, but we had another one earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to the information I received from my colleagues it was stopped at 1.58.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the first time. The second time, I think it was close to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other one is 1.59.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you said you played all of it, so let's look at the last 6 seconds as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, I will try to be as efficient as possible. According to our investigation, the person that you identified yesterday during the direct examination as the interpreter who interpreted for you and General Mladic was Gajic Ljubodrag. He's a member of the special brigade of the police, not the army. He was forcibly mobilised in Serbia. He testified before the court in Bosnia and Herzegovina and he said that he never carried out any conversation with you and General Mladic on the 12th. So that is what I am putting to you. I want to confront you with that in respect of what you've been telling us so far. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is not the correct position, because as far as I know - and even on video you are seeing it's him - I was discussing with him, with that man with a blue flak jacket. And even after that we would go together to General Mladic's place, you know, wherever he was, and he would tell him the same thing. But that does not mean that he was the interpreter for the BSA. I'm not saying that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you introduced a lot of assumed facts. You put them to the witness. The witness says that it's not correct. That's where it ends. The Chamber is, of course, not in any position at this moment to verify whether your information is accurate or not. Let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I'm not going to deal with it any longer because we will work on it in other ways. I will end by putting a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that at one point in time you informed General Mladic that in the building there were a great many people. Can you tell the Trial Chamber how many people there were there? What is your estimate?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, at that particular moment I did not know how many, but there were definitely over 1.000 people, according to my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are you then talking about the premises or the house itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please. Next question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then let us please take a look at a document, 65 ter 19814. It was used during the examination of the previous witness. Can we have page 40 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I am going to ask you to take a look and see what the representative of Doctors Without Borders said in relation to this particular information. So 65 ter document 19814, page 40. In this document Ms. Christina Schmitz informs her superiors - and that was on the 12th of July, the day that we are discussing - that 35 men were detained in a house and that they were being treated well. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this have any effect on your estimation that at the time when you talked to General Mladic there were approximately 1.000 men in the house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do object to the question because I think it's misleading to the witness. Mr. Stojanovic hasn't laid a foundation to establish that the house that's reflected here is the house that the witness is discussing in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please try to explore in terms of time and place, et cetera, unless the witness would have already a -- an answer to your question. Mr. Kingori, there was a report about 35 men being guarded in one house. Any comment on that or any knowledge of a house in which 35 people were guarded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for this particular one, I do not know which house she was referring to because I know there was several houses that had people in. I've talked about that white house. There was also another white house where some men were being taken behind and killed, and maybe Christina had another house that she was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you further want to explore the matter, then please do it in detail as far as time and place is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again about the 12th of July. You said that at one point General Mladic conceded to go to the white house and to look at the situation there. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At your request, was it possible for Mr. Mladic to see at that point that so many people were, indeed, inside the house?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was possible to see, and also he offered to take me there and we did go there together with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The interpreter that you mentioned and described earlier, was he with you and General Mladic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So how could you communicate then?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought your question was on whether we were with him when we went to the white house, only that I know -- he interpreted in a way that we understood each other and we went together with General Mladic to the white house -- to that white house and saw what was happening. And in the process whatever was done there is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you did you at any point enter the ground floor of the house?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How were you then able to estimate the number of the people there if you didn't enter the house?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were able to see through the windows and other openings from up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you are aware that you have used now 35 minutes after the break where I granted 30 minutes. Could you please wind up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to conclude with this question: Now, can you tell us, this house that you call the white house, how many windows did it have on the ground floor that enabled you to see inside, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if you want to communicate with counsel, do it, please, silently and ask counsel to approach you. So if Mr. Lukic would like to hear what Mr. Mladic says, then he'll come to you I take it. The number of windows, Mr. Kingori.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can't remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honours, just to confer for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kingori, this is my last question: Did you at any point in time went around the house or did you stay in one place outside the house by the road?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, we managed to go around a bit. It is only that we could not go inside, but we managed to go slightly towards one side and come back, but we could not go inside. So not mainly from the road alone, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kingori.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with this I conclude my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Vanderpuye, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't anticipate it will be very long though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't anticipate it will be very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a relative concept, long or short.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much minutes would you ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm guessing about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15 minutes. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. If I could have D21 brought up, please, in e-court, it's formerly 65 ter 4452.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours, and I again need your assistance and instructions. The document that we used a minute ago, 65 ter 19814, was admitted into evidence through Ms. Schmitz. We are using it again today, and if you believe that I should also offer it to be admitted, then I think this is a good time to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. You say admitted through Mr. Smith? Oh, Ms. Schmitz, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Schmitz, and according to my information it was assigned number D00018.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, is -- if a document is in evidence, it is in evidence. If another party uses that, it's usually recorded by -- the in-court system. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to clarify. The document D00018 is 65 ter 25607, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That apparently then is a different number? Please sort it out, Mr. Stojanovic, and we'll hear from you after the break. Mr. Vanderpuye, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll need to go to page 3 in the English, please, and page 6 in the B/C/S. I think we've got it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Colonel Kingori, you were shown this document by Mr. Stojanovic in the cross-examination and asked about a reference in this document concerning the basis of information that you were receiving from Srebrenica, in particular whether or not it was indicated in this report. You were shown paragraphs 1, 2, and 3, and I wanted to direct your attention to the last paragraph, item number 1. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It reads: "Info received from one of our yellow cards who is in Srebrenica at the moment and with whom we are in contact with by radio ..." Can you tell us what you mean here by "yellow card" or what is meant by "yellow card"?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, "yellow card" was used to mean interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does this refer to the interpreter Suljagic who you referred to in your cross-examination a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is Emir Suljagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And would the person or unit receiving this report understand what is meant here by "yellow card"?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to show you another document which is D22. And when that one comes up we'll need to go to page 2 in the English and page 3, I believe, in the B/C/S. And what I'd like to do is direct your attention -- you were asked some questions about a meeting in Bratunac I believe on the 11th of July. And what I'd like to do is to first direct your attention to the bottom of the page in English here where you can see a reference to a meeting that was attended by an UNMO team. Now, first can you explain or do you recall this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this meeting, we went there together with DutchBat LO team to discuss with BiH and is indicated those -- all those who were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where did that meeting occur, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this occurred at the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That would be in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me refer you to page 3 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S and we'll take a look at item number 4. If we go down to the bottom of the page we'll see item number 4, and it reads that: "The BSA requested a meeting with DutchBat and UNMOs in Bratunac. However, this was refused by UNPROFOR HQ. We are further informed that the aircraft may still execute the strike ... by 1300 hours." This is on the 11th of July, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the meeting in Bratunac that you referred to during the course of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the one that we did not attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's take a look at 65 ter 4458, and we'll go to item number 4 with respect to that document as well. Here we can see that it refers to the ongoing situation as being very tense, and under item number 4 -- or, rather, [indiscernible] and shells are overflying the DutchBat compound in Potocari, and so on and so forth. And we can see under item number 4, it says: "UNMOs are still waiting to see if the meeting with the BSA, planned by the commanding officer of DutchBat to discuss the fate of the refugees and UNPROFOR personnel will take place. UNMOs plan to attend if possible." What meeting is that?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the same meeting that had been planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was that the one that was planned to take place in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will be tendering all of the -- these are also among the associated exhibits, but I will be tendering them all. So I won't offer it this at this time because there are a couple of other documents I'd like to get through first, if that's all right with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like if you use any document, I'd like to deal with that immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I can strike it from my list of associated exhibits because they're not purely associated exhibits anymore. So now 4458, UNMO report, update, date 11 of July. Any objections against admission? No objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4458 becomes Exhibit P37, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 4436.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In relation to a number of questions that were put to you concerning your interaction with General Mladic, you were asked whether or not you recorded these conversations or otherwise noted them or whether they appeared in video. I do want to ask you about this one in particular. Under item number 2 it refers to General Mladic giving an assurance that: "... the convoy was acceptable so there should not be any problem with the convoy in Zvornik and Yellow Bridge." Do you recall the context in which this information was communicated to you or your team?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was a communication concerning the UNHCR convoy which had been scheduled to arrive much, much earlier, but was delayed by lack of authority from the BSA to get into the enclave. But here General Mladic is giving us a -- the consent that it will actually be allowed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did that occur after you had information that the convoy had been stopped, in fact?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it was a medical convoy, as indicated in this report?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next para is indicated that it had been stopped at Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to take you -- I'd like to draw your attention to item number 5 in this report, and there you will see that it reads that: "The number of BiH soldiers that are taken POW," prisoners of war, "by the BSA is not known yet but General Mladic told the UNMO team and the commanding officer of DutchBat that the BiH are having several hundreds of dead soldiers in the area of the Bandera Triangle ..." Do you recall the in context in which this information was communicated to your team?

utterances.speaker: JOSEPH KINGORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.
